retained_skill: Design and validate an extended Euclidean algorithm that computes modular inverses, including coefficient updates and normalization, on a stack VM.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts spend nearly the entire episode hand-encoding instructions, recalculating absolute jump offsets, and rewriting generators; their first executable programs have malformed encodings, stack errors, bad jumps, or wrong outputs, and none submits before its limit.
change: Repair the contradictory PUSH byte-order comment, and place structural help in the original environment: a small generic assembler module that emits VM instructions and resolves symbolic labels. This removes manual byte serialization and jump-offset bookkeeping (roughly turns 2 through the final turn in every attempt) while leaving the extended-Euclid state, update order, loop, normalization, and validation decisions wholly to the student. The original signal retained is running the resulting bytecode in the provided VM and reacting to its output/errors.
restore: A later hardening can remove /app/assembler.py and its removable instruction paragraph, returning byte emission and absolute-address bookkeeping without changing the mathematical task.
prediction: The change addresses repeated hand-written byte emitters and stale numeric jump targets. With encoding and label fixups handled, some attempts will next implement and test their extended-Euclid recurrence instead of rewriting generators; observing multiple correct nontrivial inputs before submission supports this, while another 0/12 group still ending in assembler rewrites or jump-address debugging refutes it.
